title: Michelangelo guessed Laocoön’s missing arm was bent back. In 1905 it turned up

cover.alt: The marble Laocoön group in the Vatican: a bearded man and two youths writhing in the coils of serpents, the man’s right arm bent back behind his head.

body: This ancient marble group, showing the Trojan priest Laocoön and his sons attacked by sea serpents, was dug up in a vineyard in Rome in 1506. Pope Julius II sent Giuliano da Sangallo and Michelangelo to see it, and Sangallo declared it the Laocoön that Pliny the Elder mentions, which it very likely is. Laocoön’s right arm was missing. Michelangelo suggested it had been bent back over the shoulder, but others thought an arm stretched outwards was more fitting, and from 1532 one stayed on the statue for centuries. In 1905 Ludwig Pollak found a bent marble arm in Rome, and in 1957 the Vatican decided it was the original.

slides.alt: Baccio Bandinelli’s marble copy of the Laocoön in the Uffizi, the priest’s right arm raised up and outstretched as he grips a serpent.
slides.caption: The arm that might have been: Baccio Bandinelli’s copy of the ancient Laocoön statue, about 1525, now in the Uffizi in Florence, reaches up and out.

slides.heading: Two ideas for a lost arm

left.label: Michelangelo
left.text: The missing right arm had originally been bent back over the shoulder.

right.label: The restorers
right.text: An arm stretched outwards was more appropriate. The sculptor Montorsoli fixed a straight one to the statue in 1532.

slides.heading: 450 years of a missing arm
slides.note: In the 1980s the group was taken apart and rebuilt with the arm Ludwig Pollak found.

slides.heading: Three belong to the 1506 story. Which doesn’t?
slides.explanation: Pollak found the arm in 1905. The statue came up in De Fredis’s vineyard, and Pope Julius II sent Sangallo and Michelangelo to see it.

slides.label: height of the marble group, now in the Vatican Museums
slides.text: Suggested dates for it range from 200 BC to the AD 70s, and scholars still debate whether it is an original or a copy.

slides.question: Where did Ludwig Pollak find the missing arm in 1905?
options: In a builder’s yard in Rome
slides.explanation: In a builder’s yard in Rome, close to where the group had been found. A drill hole in one piece aligned perfectly with the other.
